(men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] | highlights = *First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2018) }} '''Jerome Robinson''' (born February 22, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL). He played [[college basketball]] with the [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College Eagles]].{{cite web|title=Jerome Robinson - Basketball Recruiting - Player Profiles - ESPN|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/203561/jerome-robinson|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 4, 2018}} He was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the first round of the [[2018 NBA draft]] with the 13th overall pick. ==College career== Robinson was not ranked as a high school recruit and had trouble receiving offers from Power-5 programs from [[Needham B. Broughton High School]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. Boston College assistant coach [[Scott Spinelli]], who is known for finding diamonds in the rough, was the only representative of a Power-5 school to offer Robinson. As a freshman, Robinson averaged 11.7 points, 4 rebounds and 3 assists per game for the 2015–16 season. As a sophomore, he averaged 18.7 points, 4 rebounds, and 3.4 assists per game. During his junior year, he averaged 20.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game and was named All [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] First Team with 14 [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ACC Player of the Year]] votes.{{Cite news|url=http://www.theacc.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-acc-announces-all-conference-team-postseason-awards.aspx|title=ACC Announces All-Conference Team, Postseason Awards|access-date=April 4, 2018}} Additionally, he was an [[Associated Press]] honorable mention All-American. He scored a career-high 46 points in a loss at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] on February 6. After the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent to preserve his collegiate eligibility.{{cite news|last1=Weitzer|first1=Nate|title=BC's Jerome Robinson and Ky Bowman declare for NBA Draft|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/colleges/2018/04/04/jerome-robinson-and-bowman-declare-for-nba-draft/548XAy60JO2wqe0UeHixeP/story.html|access-date=April 5, 2018|work=[[Boston Globe]]|date=April 5, 2018}} On April 28, 2018, he hired an agent with CAA sports thus ending his eligibility.{{cite web|title=Jerome Robinson to stay in NBA Draft|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/272747/jerome-robinson-to-stay-in-nba-draft.html|website=Sportando|access-date=April 29, 2018|date=April 28, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622055958/https://sportando.basketball/en/usa/nba/272747/jerome-robinson-to-stay-in-nba-draft.html|archive-date=June 22, 2018|url-status=dead}} Robinson became the first ever lottery draft pick out of Boston College. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Clippers (2018–2020)=== On June 21, 2018, Robinson was selected with the thirteenth overall pick by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in the [[2018 NBA draft]].{{cite magazine |last1=Lander |first1=Ben |title=Clippers Select Jerome Robinson With No. 13 Pick in 2018 NBA Draft |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/06/21/jerome-robinson-2018-draft-grades |access-date=January 11, 2020 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 21, 2018}} Robinson scored a career-high 21 points in a win versus the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on November 17, 2019.{{cite news |title=Clippers' Jerome Robinson: Scores career-high 21 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-jerome-robinson-scores-career-high-21-points/ |access-date=January 11, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=November 17, 2019}} ===Washington Wizards (2020–2021)=== On February 6, 2020, Robinson was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a 3-team trade, involving the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-jerome-robinson-clippers-isaiah-thomas-issuf-sanon|title=Wizards acquire Jerome Robinson from Clippers|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020|access-date=February 6, 2020}} On April 8, 2021, Robinson was waived by the Wizards after 38 appearances.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-waive-jerome-robinson|title=Wizards waive Jerome Robinson|work=NBA.com|date=April 8, 2021|access-date=April 8, 2021}} ===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2022–2024)=== On January 5, 2022, Robinson was acquired by the [[Santa Cruz
